sections.section_title: Pathophysiology and Background of Immune-Mediated Necrotizing Myopathy (IMNM)
sections.description: This section establishes the foundational medical knowledge required to understand the case, focusing on the nature of IMNM, its associated biomarkers, and the emerging profile of GLP-1 receptor agonists.
subtopics: Definition and clinical features of Immune-Mediated Necrotizing Myopathy (IMNM)
Pathogenesis of necrotizing myofibers and inflammatory infiltrates
Role of autoantibodies: HMGCR and SRP associations
The challenge of 'seronegative' IMNM: Diagnostic implications and potential triggers
Overview of GLP-1 receptor agonists: Mechanism of action and known skeletal muscle effects
Distinguishing drug-induced rhabdomyolysis from autoimmune myopathy

sections.section_title: Clinical Presentation: Acute Reaction and Progressive Myopathy
sections.description: This section details the patient's clinical trajectory, starting from the initial acute reaction to semaglutide and the subsequent progressive development of muscle-related symptoms.
subtopics: Patient history: Metabolic comorbidities (Obesity, NAFLD, Hypertension)
Acute adverse reaction to semaglutide: Gastrointestinal distress and secondary acute renal failure
Delayed progression: Development of proximal muscle weakness, dysphagia, and dysphonia
Temporal relationship: Analyzing the 4-month window between drug exposure and clinical deterioration
Physical examination findings in severe proximal myopathy

sections.description: This section explores the multi-modal diagnostic approach, including laboratory investigations, imaging, and histopathology, while explaining the reasoning used to reach a definitive diagnosis.
subtopics: Laboratory markers: Interpreting Creatine Kinase (CK) trends and transaminase elevations
Autoantibody profiling: Interpreting negative myositis panels and isolated SS-B positivity
Diagnostic imaging: MRI findings of muscular edema and cardiac evaluation
Histopathology: Analyzing muscle biopsy for necrotic fibers, myophagocytosis, and MAC deposition
Differential Diagnosis: Ruling out rhabdomyolysis, toxic myopathy, and standard polymyositis
Causality assessment: Applying WHO-Uppsala Monitoring Centre criteria to drug-induced myopathy

sections.description: This section covers the pharmacological interventions used to treat the IMNM and the patient's subsequent recovery and long-term follow-up.
subtopics: Acute management: Pulse methylprednisolone for severe muscle involvement
Adjunctive therapy: The role and administration of Intravenous Immunoglobulin (IVIG)
Steroid tapering and long-term monitoring
Clinical recovery: Restoration of baseline functional status and normalization of CK levels
Resolution of imaging abnormalities and cardiac findings

sections.description: The final section synthesizes the case into broader clinical lessons, highlighting the importance of monitoring for rare but severe adverse effects of new metabolic medications.
subtopics: Identifying IMNM vs. Rhabdomyolysis: Key clinical discriminators (time course and treatment response)
The importance of muscle biopsy in seronegative cases
Pharmacovigilance: Recognizing the role of GLP-1 agonists as potential triggers for autoimmune myopathy
Patient counseling: Education on recognizing early symptoms of myopathy during metabolic treatment
Future directions: Identifying predisposing factors for drug-induced IMNM
